alternatives.label: Language, organisations & persuasive communication
alternatives.concept: A broad communication programme joining rhetoric and linguistic style with leadership, consumer communication, media interpretation and empirical research. It materially responds to language and organisational communication, while differing from Radboud’s specialist intercultural, conversation-analysis and compulsory-thesis sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: A broad communication programme joining rhetoric and linguistic style with leadership, consumer communication, media interpretation and empirical research. It materially responds to language and organisational communication, while differing from Radboud’s specialist intercultural, conversation-analysis and compulsory-thesis sequence.
progression: Actual current offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass; first-year PPD,24unique180EC,fourperterm,advancedminimum. Foundationalrhetoric/data/empiricalmethods preferredbeforeadvancedapplications; no inventedformalprerequisites.

alternatives.label: Communication for social impact
alternatives.concept: A public communication route connecting rhetoric and media analysis with climate, health, social movements, environmental justice and civil society. Its empirical and organisational courses support scrutiny of persuasive messages and communication for change.
alternatives.labelReason: A public communication route connecting rhetoric and media analysis with climate, health, social movements, environmental justice and civil society. Its empirical and organisational courses support scrutiny of persuasive messages and communication for change.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad programme, this route replaces nine courses in business, marketing, data and AI with climate, public health, media representation, social movements, environmental justice and civil-society study; those differences follow the evidenced social-impact direction.
progression: Actual current offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass; first-year PPD,24unique180EC,fourperterm,advancedminimum. Foundationalrhetoric/data/empiricalmethods preferredbeforeadvancedapplications; no inventedformalprerequisites.

alternatives.label: Human and digital communication
alternatives.concept: A communication programme combining rhetoric, media interpretation and human language processing with empirical research and computational text methods. Programming, neural networks, text generation and model evaluation support inquiry into human and digital communication; they do not reproduce the whole specialist chatbot or conversation-analysis curriculum. Cultural representation and organisational behaviour provide context for evaluating communication between people and digital systems.
alternatives.labelReason: A communication programme combining rhetoric, media interpretation and human language processing with empirical research and computational text methods. Programming, neural networks, text generation and model evaluation support inquiry into human and digital communication; they do not reproduce the whole specialist chatbot or conversation-analysis curriculum. Cultural representation and organisational behaviour provide context for evaluating communication between people and digital systems.
alternatives.distinctness: This route substitutes specialised programming, AI decision-making, neural networks, visual analysis, psycholinguistics and philosophy of mind for much of the broad programme's international business, marketing, organisational psychology and qualitative-methods strand. It also differs from the social-impact route by a sustained technical and cognitive sequence.
progression: Actual current offerings and earlier formal prerequisites pass; first-year PPD,24unique180EC,fourperterm,advancedminimum. Foundationalrhetoric/data/empiricalmethods preferredbeforeadvancedapplications; no inventedformalprerequisites.

routeSelection.route: Dutch-taught Communication and Information Studies specialisation; non-abroad pathway; Online Reputation restricted choice
routeSelection.basis: Exact Dutch CIW target under current OER; no foreign stay selected. Among three equally5-EC specialist B3 choices, first-listed Online Reputation is the neutral tie-break, independent of UCR match.

selection.assessment: The broad route covers communication, organisations, media, persuasion and research. Social impact and human/digital communication have independently evidenced organising logics and material curricular consequences; the pairs differ by nine, ten and sixteen courses respectively, exceeding the four-course floor. Multilingual/intercultural business communication is another evidenced direction but no fourth programme can be included. Currentcontentreview retains3substantivedirections with[9, 9, 14]differentcourses. notes.text: Radboud offers sustained study of multilingual organisational communication, specialist communication analysis, digital communication and a compulsory bachelor thesis. UCR can combine rhetoric, media, organisational study, social issues and digital methods in different ways, but these schedules do not replicate the full specialist sequence or required thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud’s Communication and Information Studies examines language and communication between people, organisations and digital systems. Students study persuasion, organisational and intercultural communication, discourse, digital media and qualitative and quantitative research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: These UCR programmes combine language and persuasion with organisational study, social issues or human and digital communication. They offer meaningful related study, including partial intercultural, interaction and computational-language methods. They differ from Radboud’s specialist communication-analysis and online-reputation courses, cross-cultural English study and compulsory bachelor thesis.

componentNotes.y3-misinfo: One of three restricted choices; Online Reputation is shown here.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Compulsory 10 EC thesis, begun in the second semester of year 3.
componentNotes.y2-minor-1: Choose one approved 15-EC Faculty of Arts minor in each semester. Each minor is a fixed package; courses from different minors cannot be mixed into a new minor.
componentNotes.y2-minor-2: The second approved 15-EC Faculty of Arts minor completes 30 EC of minor study. Minors from other faculties belong in free elective space.
componentNotes.y3-free: 30 EC of bachelor-level study to broaden the degree. Courses belonging to another specialisation of this same degree cannot fill this space; foreign courses require prior examination-board approval.
componentNotes.y1-research: Mentorship, Dutch academic language proficiency and later mentorship/development obligations add no credits. Attendance and required practical assignments apply. The normal first-year study-advice threshold is 45 EC, subject to personal circumstances.
